nodes.summary: Let $\delta$ be a real number. A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is admissible at level $\delta$ when it is a zero-mean $H^2$ function, its gradient energy equals $1$, and its Laplacian energy equals $\delta$.
nodes.title: Conditionally admissible functions

nodes.summary: For a real number $\delta$, this is the set of extended real numbers $u(0)^2$, where $u$ ranges over the continuous functions $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that are conditionally admissible at level $\delta$.
nodes.title: Squared values at the origin of admissible functions

nodes.summary: Let $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous and let $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ be a frequency. The Fourier coefficient of $u$ at $k$ is $a_k = 2\pi c_k$, where $c_k = \int_{[0,1]^2} u(2\pi y)\, e^{-2\pi i\, k \cdot y}\, dy$ is the Fourier coefficient of the rescaled function $y \mapsto u(2\pi y)$ on the unit torus with respect to normalized Haar measure. Equivalently,…
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients on the torus

nodes.summary: For a continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$, the frequency ratio is the Laplacian energy of $u$ divided by the gradient energy of $u$.
nodes.title: Frequency ratio

nodes.summary: For a frequency $k = (k_1, k_2) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the frequency weight is $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$, the squared frequency of the mode $e^{i k \cdot x}$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.
nodes.title: Squared frequency

nodes.summary: The frequencies are the elements of the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, that is, the pairs $k = (k_1, k_2)$ of integers; they index the Fourier modes of the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.
nodes.title: Integer frequencies

nodes.summary: For a continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, the gradient energy is $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |k|^2 \, |a_k|^2$, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$; the sum is taken to be $0$ when the series diverges.
nodes.title: Gradient energy

nodes.summary: A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$ is in $H^2$ when the series $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} (1 + |k|^2)^2 \, |a_k|^2$ converges, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$.
nodes.title: Functions in $H^2$

nodes.summary: A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a zero-mean $H^2$ function when it is in $H^2$ and its mean is $0$.
nodes.title: Zero-mean $H^2$ functions

nodes.summary: For a continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, the Laplacian energy is $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |k|^4 \, |a_k|^2$, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$; the sum is taken to be $0$ when the series diverges.
nodes.title: Laplacian energy

nodes.summary: For a continuous function $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, its mean is $\int_{(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2} u(2\pi y)\, d\mu(y)$, where $\mu$ is the normalized Haar measure on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ and $y \mapsto 2\pi y$ is the inverse of the rescaling to unit period.
nodes.title: Mean of a function on the torus

nodes.summary: For real $\delta$, the remainder is the extended real number $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$, where $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.
nodes.title: Logarithmic remainder

nodes.summary: The sharp remainder is the supremum, in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the remainders $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$ over all real $\delta \ge 1$, where $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.
nodes.title: Sharp logarithmic remainder

nodes.summary: The set of extended real numbers $R(\delta)$ for all real $\delta \ge 1$, where $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$ is the logarithmic remainder and $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.
nodes.title: Set of remainder values

nodes.summary: For real $\delta$, $\theta(\delta)$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the conditional point values at $\delta$: the numbers $u(0)^2$ over all continuous $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that are conditionally admissible at $\delta$, that is, of mean zero and in $H^2$ with gradient energy $1$ and Laplace energy $\delta$.
nodes.title: Conditional supremum of the squared value at the origin

nodes.summary: The two-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, the product of two copies of the circle $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: The torus of period $2\pi$

nodes.summary: For a real constant $L$, the bound with constant $L$ holds when, for every continuous $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that has mean zero and lies in $H^2$, has positive gradient energy $E(u)$, and, writing $\Delta(u)$ for its Laplace energy, has frequency ratio $\Lambda(u) = \Delta(u)/E(u) \ge 1$, every point $x$ of the torus satisfies…
nodes.title: Uniform logarithmic remainder bound

nodes.summary: The measure on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ that is the product of two copies of the Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Normalized Haar measure on the unit torus

nodes.summary: For a continuous function $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, its unit representative is the continuous function $\tilde u : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $\tilde u(y) = u(2\pi y)$, the composition of $u$ with the inverse of the rescaling to unit period, with its real values regarded as complex numbers.
nodes.title: A function on the torus as a function on the unit torus

nodes.summary: The homeomorphism from the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ onto the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ that sends $(x_1, x_2)$ to $(x_1/(2\pi), x_2/(2\pi))$.
nodes.title: Rescaling the torus to unit period
